study.title: Psalm 3 Trust in God amidst Rebellion
study.overview: This psalm presents David fleeing, surrounded by opposition and humiliation, but without losing confidence in the Lord. The text advances from the cry before the enemies to the confession that God is protection, hears prayer, sustains the sleep of the afflicted, defeats the wicked, and ultimately grants salvation and blessing to his people. The central tension of the psalm is this: circumstances seem to deny security, but faith states that salvation belongs to the LORD.

outline.title: The crowd of adversaries and the accusation of abandonment
outline.explanation: David regrets that his enemies multiplied and that many have cruelly concluded that God had forsaken him. The psalm begins with real pain and the attempt of enemies to turn the crisis into proof of divine rejection.

outline.title: The Lord as a shield, glory and sustainer
outline.explanation: The answer of faith contrasts with the voice of the adversaries: God is a shield, restores the honor of the servant and hears his cry. Trust reaches the point of David sleeping and awakening in peace, because he recognizes that the LORD sustains him.

outline.title: Courage, request for intervention and final confession
outline.explanation: Even surrounded by many, David does not surrender to fear. He asks God to act, recognizes that victory comes from the Lord Himself and ends with a blessing upon the people of God.

study.context: The title connects the psalm to a period of David's escape before his son Absalom. The given notes associate this scenario with the rebellion recorded in 2 Samuel 15-18, but the psalm itself does not depend on many historical details to be understood: it shows a anointed one of God in distress, suffering internal and external opposition. The value of the context is to illuminate the experience of disorder, humiliation, and wait for divine action.
study.theology: The psalm teaches that God's faithfulness is not annulled by the contrary appearance of circumstances. The enemies interpret the crisis as proof of abandonment; however, David interprets reality in the light of the character of God. The LORD is a shield, that is, active protection; he is the one who raises his head, that is, restores dignity and hope; he is the one who answers prayer and sustains rest; and he is also the one who saves completely. The text also shows that true faith does not exclude the urgent request: David trusts and at the same time pleads with intervention. Finally, salvation is presented as belonging to the LORD, not to human power, and the blessing upon the people depends on this divine grace.

scholarViews.insight: The psalm contrasts the opposition of the enemies with the provision of the LORD; God is a shield for his people and transforms defeat and shame into victory and glory.
In recalling his escape before Absalom, the psalm shows that, even in great sorrow, David was able to compose a prayer of comfort and security under divine protection.
The final declaration teaches that salvation belongs only to the LORD; from him they proceed help and deliverance, and the blessing upon his people remains for his mercy.

questions: When I am tempted to measure the presence of God only by the size of my problems, how does this psalm correct my vision?
What does it mean, in practice, to say that God is my shield and what raises my head?
Instead of seeking revenge or control, how can I learn to deliver the cause to the Lord and rest in it?
study.practice: Take to God, in direct prayer, the situation that today threatens your peace. Name the fears, confess that salvation comes from the Lord and ask him for courage to rest without bitterness or revenge. Then choose a concrete attitude of trust: a reconciler conversation, a patient decision or an act of worship before bedtime, remembering that God supports his servant.
study.uncertainty: The notes quote the scene of Absalom and the rebellion described in 2 Samuel, but the psalm itself only indicates David's escape. There are also limits in understanding the word 'Selelá', because the notes recognize that its exact meaning is uncertain; therefore, any detailed explanation should be treated with caution.
